props.title: The Secret War of Harry Frigg

sections.content: The Secret War of Harry Frigg (1968) represents a curious intersection of WWII comedy and prison escape films, starring Paul Newman at the height of his charismatic powers. Released in the same era as more serious POW films like The Great Escape (1963) and Von Ryan's Express (1965), Frigg takes a decidedly lighter approach. Newman plays a professional escape artist from military prisons who's promoted to Private First Class and sent to liberate five Allied generals from an Italian villa-turned-prison. The film showcases the late 1960s trend of mixing war movie tropes with comedy, similar to What Did You Do in the War, Daddy? (1966) and The Secret War of Walter Mitty (1947).

sections.content: The film's Italian villa setting and romantic subplot with Sylva Koscina echoes the lighter European war comedies of the period, like Operation Crossbow (1965) and Castle Keep (1969). Director Jack Smight, who would later direct Midway (1976), brings a breezy touch to the material that distinguishes it from grittier WWII films of the era. Newman's performance as Frigg continues his string of charming antiheroes from films like Cool Hand Luke (1967) and The Sting (1973).

The film's approach to military bureaucracy and incompetent leadership reflects the growing cynicism toward authority in late 1960s cinema. While not as biting as **M*A*S*H(1970) or Catch-22 (1970), it shares their irreverent view of military hierarchy and protocol. The comedic treatment of imprisonment and escape would influence later films likeHogan's Heroes** (TV, 1965-1971) and Victory (1981). SUBHEAD: Comedy in World War II Cinema

sections.content: The late 1960s marked a significant shift in how Hollywood portrayed World War II, moving from straight heroic narratives to more complex and often comedic takes. The Secret War of Harry Frigg fits into this transformation alongside films like Where Eagles Dare (1968) and The Dirty Dozen (1967), which mixed action with dark humor and anti-authoritarian themes.
